chapters.html:
The second hand on the little wall clock above the bar seemed louder than the clinking of glasses or the low hum of chatter drifting across the restaurant, as if conspiring to remind Mydei of every passing second, every slow minute, every humiliating moment that stretched out in front of her like a thread pulled too thin. She sat with her back perfectly straight, shoulders tight beneath the silky fall of her blonde hair, one hand resting on her glass and the other tapping silently against her thigh, as though by some small act of rhythm she might keep herself together, stave off the creeping suspicion that she had been made a fool of.

Seven o’clock sharp, she had been here. 

Seven o’clock sharp, she had smiled politely at the waiter, ordered a drink to keep herself from looking like a lost child, and opened her phone to double-check the messages, the ones where Castorice and Cipher had sworn this date would be worth it, so worth it, Mydei, she’s gorgeous, sweet, a bit crazy and totally your type, trust us just this once, trust us.

Seven o’clock sharp, and now it was eight-twenty-six, and her untouched glass of water had gone warm, and her iced tea was down to a sad scattering of cubes floating in amber, and her phone screen had gone dark after the last desperate message, Are you on your way?

Read at 7:05. 

No fucking reply.

She could feel the pity radiating off the waitstaff, little glances slid in her direction when they thought she wasn’t looking, the soft curve of the waitress’s mouth tilting into something gentle, sympathetic, unbearable. The couple at the next table over had exchanged whispers too, the man’s gaze darting toward her before being elbowed in the ribs by his date, who shook her head and muttered something that made his ears go pink.

Mydei wanted to fold into herself like paper, vanish into her chair, anything but sit here under the quiet, merciless spotlight of being the woman who had been stood up.

The humiliation had an odd taste, bitter, metallic, and stubbornly clinging to the back of her throat, and she kept swallowing hard as if she might push it down with the last of her pride and dignity.

This is fine. It’s fine, not the end of the world. I’ll give her until eight-thirty. After that, I’ll leave with dignity, head held high, and I’ll never, ever let Castorice and Cipher talk me into one of their ridiculous schemes again, she thought, tucking a long strand of hair behind her ear.

If she closed her eyes and imagined really hard, she could already hear their voices. Cipher, sharp in disbelief, two seconds away from ruining the poor girl's life in any way possible, and Castorice, trying for soothing but failing, a hard edge in her otherwise gentle voice.

Mydei pressed her palms to her thighs, smoothed down her skirt, tilted her chin a little higher. “It's not bad luck,” she muttered under her breath, “It's her fault, not mine. They're the ones to set me up, and I'm going to hold this over their heads for the rest of my life.”

The waitress drifted by again, refilling water with a little too much care, and Mydei gave her the brightest, most brittle smile she could manage. Just four minutes left, she told herself. Four minutes, and then she could go home, cry into Castorice’s hoodie while Cipher bought out the cheap ice cream, and order takeout and let her best friends wallow in the guilt of her tears for weeks.

But as the clock hand inched toward the half hour, as she pushed her empty glass aside and gathered her courage to stand, the sound of a chair scraping startled her. Someone slid into the seat across from her with the smooth, unhurried confidence of a person who had absolutely every right to be there.

“Sorry I’m so late, babe,” the woman said, her voice low and bright, “Traffic was a nightmare.”

Mydei froze, the world narrowing into a single frame, her eyes flicking up and locking onto a pair of the bluest eyes she had ever seen. Not blue like the sky, because they were too soft and they weren't blue like water, because water was too ordinary. They were blue like glass struck through with sunlight, sharp and vivid and unyielding.

Her brain tripped over itself, unable to reconcile the sight in front of her: tall, broad-shouldered, (possibly taller than her, which was an impressive feat), dressed in a dark jacket over a distinctive blue hoodie of their University, short white hair cut into a sharp wolfcut that framed a strong jaw, and a look, that was steady, almost amused, but undercut by something gentler.

The woman leaned forward slightly, lowering her voice as though sharing a secret. “My name’s Phainon. Just… play along, alright? Whoever stood you up is a total asshole, no offense.”

Mydei’s heart stuttered, her throat catching on a soundless reply. Any kindness, unexpected and bold, had a way of undoing her quicker than cruelty ever could. For a moment, she could only blink at her, heat rushing to her cheeks, every carefully rehearsed exit line evaporating into nothing.

“Phainon,” she echoed faintly, as if saying the name might tether her back to reality, and then, belatedly, something clicked. “Wait, Phainon? That Phainon?”

An eyebrow arched, and the faintest smirk tugged at the corner of the woman’s mouth. “Depends on how many you know?”

“My friend Castorice mentioned you,” Mydei admitted, dazed. “You worked together on a project once, right? She said you were–” She caught herself before she could say anything foolish, pressing her lips together. Castorice had not gushed, not really, had only mentioned Phainon in passing, the way one mentions a competent group member who actually showed up on time, which in university circles was as good as sainthood, and her voice was approving, saying something along the lines of his Phainon made her feel included, always respecting her boundaries. But even that small detail felt impossibly heavy now, as though she should have been warned, or even prepared for someone like this.

The smirk softened into a genuine smile, as her blue eyes brightened, “Oh, yeah, Castorice! She's really smart, and to be honest, I do kinda miss her company at times, and the fact that she's covered in butterflies everywhere.”

Something in Mydei cracked then, a laugh bubbling up from nerves and disbelief and the sharp, dizzying relief of not being alone anymore, “The last part is very… accurate.”

She hadn’t known, hadn’t expected, and certainly hadn’t imagined that her night, which had been spiraling steadily toward lonely disaster, might suddenly tilt into something else entirely and yet here was Phainon, tall and vivid and startlingly real, sliding into her evening like she belonged there all along.

The waitress reappeared not long after Phainon had claimed her seat, eyes darting between them with a look that was no longer pitiful but quietly hopeful, as though she were watching a fragile miracle take shape in front of her.

“Will you be ordering now?” she asked, her smile a touch brighter than before, and Mydei wondered if the universe itself had conspired to keep her seated here long enough for this unexpected detour.

“Yes,” Phainon said, quick and confident, though her voice carried the faintest waver at the end, betraying nerves. She picked up the menu like someone scanning instructions for a machine she didn’t quite know how to operate, and then added, “We’ll… share something, uh, right, baby?”

Mydei nearly choked on air. The word baby, tossed so casually across the table, rang in her ears like a bell, and Phainon, tall, awkward, Phainon was looking at her with the tiniest flicker of panic in her eyes, as though she’d realized the weight of the word too late.

It was Mydei’s turn to smirk, “Of course, darling,” she said sweetly, leaning into the game.

The waitress’s smile turned positively radiant as she scribbled their order, and Mydei caught the slight curve at the corner of her mouth, the look of a woman who’d decided this evening just might have a happy ending.

When they were alone again, Mydei folded her hands under her chin, tilting her head with mock-serious curiosity, “So, Phainon, do you often rescue women from tragic nights and pretend to be their dates, or am I just lucky?”

Phainon cleared her throat, ears tinged pink. “I, uh, I just saw you sitting here and… I figured no one should have to go through that. You looked–” She paused, eyes flicking anywhere but Mydei’s, before finishing quickly, “–like you deserved better.”

The blush had spread from her ears to her neck, creeping down under the collar of her hoodie.

Mydei’s lips curved, warmth blossoming in her chest where humiliation had lived only minutes before, “That was almost smooth,” she teased.

Phainon groaned softly and dragged a hand down her face, before sneaking a look back at her, “Almost?”

“You ruined it by blushing.”

“I don’t blush.”

“You’re literally doing it right now.”

Phainon sank a little lower in her chair, muttering something incoherent, and Mydei laughed, a sound that felt freer and lighter than anything she’d managed all evening. It was intoxicating, the shift from despair to this giddy amusement, and she found herself leaning into it, leaning into Phainon.

“It's cute seeing you like this,” Mydei admitted with a small smirk.

Phainon blushed bright red, “Please stop teasing me,” she groaned, “Or I really would have no other option than to transfer.” 

“Transfer?” Mydei echoed, feigning shock. “From the team’s golden star? What would the basketball program do without you?”

She said it lightly, but Phainon stiffened, ears coloring again. “You… know about that?”

“Cipher mentioned it,” Mydei admitted, swirling her fork around the air. “I didn’t really think about it. Sports events were never my thing. I’m personally more of a gym girl.” She hesitated, then, inside her head, words spun faster than she could catch them. If I had known the basketball team’s ‘star’ was you, a woman, and this unfairly handsome, I would’ve been in the bleachers every week, screaming my lungs out like a diehard fan.

Aloud, she said simply, “I like working out. It helps me focus.”

Phainon blinked, tilting her head, “Wait, which gym do you go to?”

“Campus rec center, the one with the squeaky treadmills.”

“No way.” Phainon’s grin widened, and there was that faint blush again, softer now, but very endearing, “I go there too! Every morning, and you’re telling me we’ve been lifting weights within the same four walls this whole time and never noticed?”

Mydei laughed, genuine and delighted, “Apparently. Though to be fair, I’m usually in the free weights section with my headphones in. You’d have to wave in my face to get my attention.”

“I’d wave,” Phainon said before she could stop herself, then immediately flushed bright red as she coughed into her hand, trying to cover the slip, “I mean– not, like, creepily. Just– if I knew it was you.”

“You’re adorable when you’re flustered,” Mydei said, grinning.

Phainon groaned, pressing a hand over her face, “You’re enjoying this.”

“Immensely.”

The waitress passed by again at that moment, catching the tail end of their laughter. She set down fresh water with a smile that was now openly conspiratorial, the kind that said she was personally rooting for them.

Phainon waited until she left before muttering, “She’s going to tell all her coworkers about us, isn’t she?”

“Probably,” Mydei said with mock-seriousness. “We’ll be legendary here. The poor, tragic girl who was stood up, saved by the mysterious, blushing knight in a jacket.”

“That’s–” Phainon broke off, covering her eyes with her hand again as her ears went crimson. “Not fair.”

“You make it too easy,” Mydei teased, her golden eyes warm and playful now, all traces of humiliation gone, and Phainon, despite her mortification, couldn’t stop smiling.

As their food arrived, conversation unraveled easily between them. They discovered a shared love of animals, Phainon speaking fondly of her childhood farm dog Snowy, her sister’s temperamental rescue cat, while Mydei pulled up a picture of her car she raised with her parents, until she moved away for college.

“You’d like him,” she said, sliding the phone across the table.

Phainon studied the photo with a reverence that seemed out of place for a phone screen, then looked up with a small, earnest smile, “Yeah, he looks so cute and friendly.”

“Like you?”

This time, the blush returned so fast that Mydei almost felt guilty. Almost. She laughed again, delighted, and was surprised at how natural it felt to tease her, how unguarded Phainon seemed despite her intimidating exterior.

Later, when the conversation drifted to hobbies, Mydei perked up at the mention of a culinary course Phainon had once taken.

“You cook?”

“I try, I guess,” Phainon admitted, rubbing the back of her neck. “I took the class so I wouldn’t burn pasta, my sister's busy, so I try to cook as often as I can, but I made one decent risotto and thought I was a genius, but I haven’t… really kept up with it. But, I'm really good at making salads!” She finished brightly.

“Oh, I love cooking,” Mydei said eagerly, sitting forward, golden eyes bright, “It’s like therapy. I feel like I'm in control whenever I'm in the kitchen, like it's my domain.”

Phainon chuckled, and for the first time, her embarrassment seemed to fade into something steadier, more comfortable. “Guess you’ll have to teach me sometime. You know, so I don’t live off cereal.”

The words tumbled out casually enough, but as soon as they left her mouth, Phainon froze, realizing how it sounded. The blush roared back to life, “I mean– not that you have to! Obviously, just like, if you… wanted to.”

Mydei bit her lip, fighting a smile, “Are you asking me on a second date, Phainon?”

Phainon nearly knocked over her water.

The waitress, sweeping past with another table’s tray, stifled a laugh behind her hand.

And Mydei, who only an hour ago had been swallowed in humiliation, now sat across from the most endearingly awkward woman she’d ever met, her own laughter bubbling up again, not brittle this time but genuine, light, and delighted. The evening had reshaped itself entirely, and she realized with something like wonder that she didn’t want it to end.

_______

The night air greeted them like a sigh of relief, warm with the faintest edge of coolness that promised autumn waiting just around the corner. Streetlamps hummed overhead, throwing golden halos onto the pavement, and the city moved in the distance with the soft rhythm of late evening, cars humming, the occasional laughter spilling from an open bar door, the muted thud of footsteps from other couples strolling past.

Phainon shoved her hands in her jacket pockets as they stepped out of the restaurant, but she lingered just a half-second longer than necessary at Mydei’s side, as though waiting for her to declare the night officially over. Mydei, meanwhile, tightened her grip on her purse, tilting her chin up with the faintest smile tugging at her lips. The idea of returning straight to the University apartment, alone, suddenly felt like a tragedy.

“So,” Phainon said at last, voice low, almost casual. “Are you heading back?”

“I was thinking…” Mydei hesitated, glancing down the street where neon lights glowed faintly against the dark. “There’s that ice cream shop still open down the block.”

Phainon blinked, then chuckled, “Really? That’s funny cuz I was just about to suggest the same thing.”

They exchanged a look, half conspiratorial, half relieved, and without another word, fell into step together.

_______

The shop was nearly empty, a sleepy place with pastel walls and the faint hum of an old freezer. The bell over the door jingled as they entered, and the girl behind the counter greeted them with the subdued brightness of someone working the late shift but secretly glad for the company.

Phainon leaned over the display case, scanning the tubs with a frown of concentration. “Vanilla,” she declared after a long pause.

“Vanilla?” Mydei repeated, incredulous and slightly offended, “Out of all these choices? Chocolate fudge, mint chip, pistachio, and you go with plain vanilla?”

“It's a classic,” Phainon defended, standing straighter. “It doesn’t need to show off.”

“Boring.” Mydei’s golden eyes danced with mischief as she gestured at the pink swirl catching her attention. “Now this, strawberry, is something sweet, bright, and refreshing.”

Phainon eyed her, lips twitching, “That sounds suspiciously like you’re describing yourself.”

Heat flickered in Mydei’s cheeks, though she masked it with a delicate lift of her brow, “And what does vanilla say about you, then?”

“That I’m–” Phainon hesitated, ears going pink again, “Simple?”

“Predictable?” Mydei supplied, grinning.

“Basic,” Phainon corrected, though her attempt at smugness faltered under the weight of her own blush.

They left the shop with cones in hand, laughter still lingering between them. Mydei licked a drip of strawberry off her thumb with deliberate slowness, catching the way Phainon’s eyes flickered quickly away, and felt a dangerous thrill curl up in her chest.

The streets had quieted more by now, the city shifting into its softer rhythms. Their shoulders brushed once, twice, before Phainon finally surrendered to the inevitable and offered her jacket when a shiver ran through Mydei. She draped it over her shoulders with a little sigh, burying herself in the warmth of it, the scent of fabric softener and something faintly like lavender clinging to the collar.

“Thanks,” she murmured, fingers curling around the edges of the sleeves.

“Anytime,” Phainon said, and it sounded almost too earnest. She hesitated, then, with careful boldness, let her arm drift around Mydei’s waist, pulling her just slightly closer as they walked.

It wasn’t dramatic, not the sweeping gestures of movies or the flamboyance of storybook romances, but there was something far more intoxicating in the subtlety of it, in the way Phainon’s body seemed to fit against hers without needing to force it, in the warmth that spread through Mydei’s chest at being held so gently, so naturally.

Neither spoke for a while as they let the silence hum between them, punctuated only by the crunch of cones and the steady rhythm of their steps.

And Mydei thought, not for the first time tonight, that perhaps humiliation was a small price to pay for this serendipitous collision, this unexpected sweetness, this sense of something beginning.

_______

By the time they reached the familiar stretch of buildings where the university apartments stood, the night had deepened into something quieter, gentler. The hum of the city felt far away now, as though the world had thinned itself into a cocoon that held only the two of them, walking close beneath the glow of streetlamps.

Phainon slowed a little when they stopped at the steps leading up to the University apartment building, reluctant to let the evening fracture into goodbye. She shifted awkwardly, hands shoved deep into her pockets again, as if keeping them there might stop her from reaching out, from betraying how badly she wanted this moment to stretch just a little longer.

“Well,” Phainon said, voice low, careful, “Guess this is your stop.”

“Guess so.” Mydei tugged her purse strap higher on her shoulder, tilting her head up ever so slightly to look up at her. The golden glow from the nearest lamp caught in her white hair, softened the sharpness of her eyes into something almost luminous.

The air between them felt charged, thick with all the things they hadn’t said, all the things they’d been circling around since that first startled meeting an hour ago.

Finally, Mydei broke the silence with a quiet, teasing lilt, “Aren’t you going to ask for my number?”

Phainon blinked, startled, then fumbled for her phone so fast she nearly dropped it. “Right! Of course I was! Yeah, I mean I was going to, no, I mean, I didn’t want to– uh– be pushy.”

Her ears were red, her voice clumsy, and Mydei’s lips curved in helpless amusement as she gently took the phone from Phainon’s hands, tapped in her number, and handed it back. “There, now you can be pushy with purpose.”

Phainon stared at the glowing digits on the screen like she’d just been handed treasure. “Thanks,” she mumbled, and then, catching herself, added more firmly, “I mean it. For tonight, too, I know it started… well, rough, but I had fun.”

“Me too,” Mydei said softly, and the sincerity in her voice made Phainon’s throat work, her usual easy confidence evaporating into something far more tentative, vulnerable.

“Then maybe–” Phainon began, but her words faltered under the weight of Mydei’s gaze.

For a heartbeat, Mydei simply looked at her, drinking in the strong line of her jaw, the way her hair framed her face, the way her brilliant blue eyes, so striking, so unflinching on the court, she imagined, now softened into wide, uncertain pools that gave her away completely. 

Puppy, she thought with sudden fondness.

And before Phainon could trip over herself any further, Mydei made her decision.

She reached up, caught Phainon lightly by the collar of her jacket, and tugged her down into a quick, soft kiss. Just a brush of lips, a spark of warmth, but enough to leave Phainon frozen in place, eyes wide, every muscle in her tall frame locking up as though struck by lightning.

When Mydei pulled back, she was already blushing, but her voice came out steady, teasing, “I really did have fun tonight.”

Phainon opened her mouth, closed it, opened it again, nothing but a strangled sound escaping. She blinked rapidly, as if trying to reboot herself, her blush burning scarlet from the tips of her ears down to her collarbone.

Mydei bit her lip to keep from laughing, watching with delight as the usually composed basketball star melted into a flustered mess in front of her.

“Goodnight, Phainon,” she whispered, and then, with a last smile, she turned and disappeared into the building, leaving the door clicking shut behind her.

Phainon remained rooted to the spot, one hand rising slowly to touch her collar where her skin still buzzed from the tug, her lips parted in wonder. She exhaled a shaky laugh, a grin tugging helplessly at her mouth until she looked for all the world like someone who had just been handed the universe in a paper bag.

_______

The door had barely clicked shut behind her when Mydei shot up the stairs two at a time, her pulse still a fluttering mess in her veins. By the time she stumbled into her bedroom, she was grinning so wide her cheeks ached as she threw her purse down, kicked off her shoes, and collapsed face-first into her pillow with a muffled squeal that quickly dissolved into helpless giggles.

She buried her burning face deeper into the pillow, kicking her legs against the mattress like a teenager, too full of fizzy happiness to contain herself.

The commotion must have carried, because a second later, the door slammed open.

“Mydei?” Castorice’s voice was soft, but her eyes were alight with curiosity. Cipher leaned in right behind her, already smirking.

Mydei jolted upright, hugging her pillow to her chest. “Do you two know how to knock?”

“Not when you come home squealing like that,” Cipher said, sliding onto the edge of the bed uninvited as she narrowed her eyes dramatically. “Spill. Now.”

Mydei pressed her lips together, feigning nonchalance, “All I’m going to say is, don’t ever set me up on another blind date again. Ever.”

Both Castorice and Cipher froze, wide-eyed, then traded a look of joint horror. 

“Oh Titans, was it that bad?” Castorice asked, biting her lip.

“No,” Mydei said quickly, and immediately cursed herself when heat rushed back to her cheeks. She buried her face in the pillow again, muffling the words, “It wasn’t bad at all, I swear.”

Cipher’s eyes widened, then gleamed with wicked glee. “Wait, wait, hold up.” She leaned closer, sing-songing, “You’re blushing. You’re blushing.”

“I am not!” Mydei snapped, which would’ve been more convincing if her ears hadn’t turned scarlet at that exact moment, but she also did have a bone to pick with both of them.

Mydei clutched the pillow to her chest. “She didn't even show up! That woman you set me up with! But, then Phainon walked in!”

Both women blinked as Castorice’s mouth fell open ever so slightly. “Wait, Phainon walked in?”

Cipher gasped so loudly it was theatrical. “Hold on, hold on, you’re telling me Phainon, the goddess of the court, the star of the basketball team, the tall, broody one with that sexy ass haircut, kissed you tonight?!”

“She didn’t–” Mydei began, but then her lips curved helplessly, the truth glowing in her expression. “Okay, fine! I kissed her! But she didn’t exactly complain.”

The room exploded with chaos. Cipher flopped back dramatically onto the bed, groaning like she’d just eaten too much sugar, “Oh Titans, you’re so disgustingly cute, I can’t take it!”

Meanwhile, Castorice leaned forward, her grin gentler, her eyes shimmering with pride. “I’m really happy for you, Mydei.”

Mydei hugged her pillow tighter, cheeks flaming but heart impossibly light.

Cipher, of course, had no mercy. She sat up again, fake-gagging into her hand, “Ugh, stop! I can literally feel the saccharine vibes dripping off you two, and my teeth are going to rot off.”

Mydei chucked the pillow at her.

“And then,” Mydei went on, like she hadn't just thrown a pillow at 30 miles per hour at a wheezing Cipher, her blush deepening, “We ate together. She was… shy, and she kept blushing whenever I teased her. It was really adorable.”

Castorice’s lips twitched, “You liked it.”

“I loved it,” Mydei admitted, hiding her face. “And when we left, we both somehow decided on ice cream. She had vanilla, and I had strawberry, and then we walked back together.”

Cipher rolled onto her back, groaning dramatically. “I can’t! You’re basically a rom-com protagonist!”

“And then…” Mydei hesitated, clutching the pillow tighter. “On the walk back, I shivered, so she gave me her jacket. And I–I kissed her on the lips.”

Cipher bolted upright, “You mean that’s her jacket you’re wearing right now?!”

Mydei froze, clutching the jacket around herself like she could hide it. “I–”

Cipher’s gasp was loud and triumphant. “It is! Oh my god! She gave you her jacket! Classic lesbian move, ten out of ten.” She dissolved into laughter, practically cackling.

“Stop it!” Mydei whined, burying her face into the jacket itself now, as if that would save her.

But then she suddenly sat up, eyes wide as another thought struck her. “Wait, I also, I also got her number.”

Both of them gasped in unison.

“You’re kidding me.” Cipher leaned forward, eyes gleaming like a predator. “You need to text her like right now, before she thinks you’re not interested.”

Castorice nodded sagely, “Cipher’s right. You need to strike while the iron’s hot.”

Mydei chewed her lip, fingers twitching nervously, but her heart fluttered all the same, the memory of Phainon’s blush when she’d kissed her goodnight fueling a giddy warmth.

_______

Meanwhile, across town, the first thing Phainon did when she entered her own apartment was nearly crash into Cyrene, who was standing in the entryway with her arms crossed, eyebrow raised.

“Well, well, well,” Cyrene said in mock sternness, arms crossed, eyes sparkling. “You’ve been gone for hours. I sent you out for ice cream, Phainon, not a pilgrimage, so unless the store moved across the city or…?” Her gaze swept over her sister’s flushed cheeks, the dazed look in her vivid blue eyes. “Oh.” A slow grin spread across her face, “Ohhh. What’s this?”

Phainon laughed, too full of bubbling energy to even be embarrassed at the knowing glint in her sister's eye, “Cyrene, you won’t believe what happened!”

Cyrene tilted her head, feigning seriousness but failing to mask her grin, “Try me.”

And so Phainon told her. She told her how she’d spotted Mydei sitting alone at the restaurant, looking sad in a way that had twisted her chest; how she couldn’t stand it, couldn’t walk past; how she’d sat down, ordered food, talked, and laughed until the sadness in Mydei’s eyes softened.

Cyrene squealed halfway through the retelling, grabbing her sister’s hands and shaking them, “You finally went on a date with the girl you’ve been mooning over for months! Do you know how insufferable you’ve been every time she walked by on campus?”

“Cyrene!” Phainon groaned, but her ears burned pink. “It wasn’t a real date. I just didn’t want her to feel stood up, and–”

“Sweetheart, you gave her your jacket,” Cyrene cut in, smug, “That’s as real as it gets, I'm afraid.”

Phainon scowled weakly as Cyrene flashed a crooked smile at her before gesturing at her to continue.

So Phainon told her about the ice cream after, about Mydei’s strawberry cone, about how the pink had looked almost made for her, and the jacket, how she’d wrapped it around Mydei’s shoulders when the evening breeze grew cooler, how beautiful she’d looked in it, how Phainon had nearly lost her composure entirely.

Her voice grew brighter, stumbling over itself in eagerness.

“Phainon.” Cyrene’s hands were pressed to her cheeks, eyes sparkling, “You’re killing me! You’re so cute! Do you hear yourself right now? It’s like I’m watching a romance novel unfold in real time!”

Phainon groaned, but couldn’t stop the laugh that broke through. “I can’t help it. She’s just– she’s–"

“My baby sister finally went on a date with the girl you’ve been crushing on for months! This is the happiest day of my life!”

“It wasn’t a real date,” Phainon protested weakly, again.

“Yes, it was!” Cyrene shot back, nearly giddy. “A jacket, ice cream and a walk home. That’s a date in every single rom-com formula ever written! The only thing that's missing is a kiss.”

Phainon’s eyes widened, her lips curving helplessly, “She did kiss me. On the lips, right at her apartment.”

Cyrene froze at the confession, “Are you serious?! Phainon, are you kidding me!? Oh my god! You two are so cute, stop making me feel like a third wheel!”

Her phone buzzed loudly from her pocket.

Both froze, then snapped their gazes to the screen at the same time.

Cyrene gasped, bouncing on her toes, “Check! It could be her!”

Phainon hastily took it out, heart hammering, and her breath hitched when she saw the name glowing there, “It’s… Mydei.”

“Open it!” Cyrene squealed.

Hands trembling, Phainon unlocked the phone. A simple message waited,

Mydei: Thank you again for tonight. And for the jacket. I’ll return it tomorrow, if you don’t mind seeing me again.

10:21

Phainon’s eyes went wide, then glazed with wonder, and she thrust the phone toward Cyrene as if she needed proof.

Cyrene clasped her hands together, eyes sparkling with glee. “She wants to see you again tomorrow. Tomorrow. Do you understand what this means?”

Phainon could only nod, dazed, puppy-like, her grin helpless and giddy, “Yeah, I get to see her again.”

Together, bent over the glowing phone, they typed back an eager reply.

With her sister’s gleeful encouragement and way too many squeals, Phainon typed back with trembling fingers, cheeks still glowing,

Phainon: Don’t worry about the jacket. I’m just glad you had fun. I did too! Can’t wait for tomorrow.

10:22

Cyrene threw herself dramatically onto the couch, clutching at her chest, “You two are going to kill me with how adorable you are.”

Phainon only smiled helplessly at her phone, heart racing like she’d just run ten miles.

_______

Campus mornings were always loud—students streaming in, chatter bouncing off the tall windows of the hallway, the smell of coffee clinging to the air. Phainon walked in with her bag slung lazily over one shoulder, still buzzing from the texts she and Mydei had exchanged late into the night, and her chest felt lighter than it had in months.

And of course, the first people she ran into were the twins.

“There she is!” Stelle practically shouted across the hallway, waving her arms like Phainon had just returned from war. She marched up, grinning wide, but stopped short as she narrowed her eyes, “Why do you look like that?”

Phainon blinked, baffled, “…Like what?”

“Like someone finally got kissed,” Caelus answered, sauntering in with the same mischievous smirk, his golden eyes gleaming with trouble.

Phainon nearly choked, “Wha–?”

Stelle circled her like a shark, scrutinizing her flushed cheeks, the faint curve tugging at her lips, the faint dreamy glaze in her eyes. “Yup! You're right, Caelus, she totally kissed someone, or got kissed by a pretty woman. I knew it!”

“I didn’t–” Phainon tried, but Stelle cut her off, wagging her finger in her face as if Phainon were some disobedient child.

“Don’t lie to me, girl. I’ve known you ever since all three of us nearly got kidnapped by our estranged dad and his merry band of totally suspicious kids.”

“Who were old enough to be our parents. Also, to be honest, I'm pretty sure that Zephyro guy was guilty of third-degree murder.” Caelus mused.

“Totally. I'm pretty sure Phantylia is guilty of blackmail. What do you think, Phainon?”

Phainon groaned, dragging a hand down her face, “I thought we had all agreed to just forget about that incident, you two are way too interested and chill about the fact that your possible dad is guilty of murder and–”

But before she could even start fully ranting, both twins’ eyes suddenly widened in perfect unison.

They weren’t looking at her anymore; they were looking past her.

Phainon stiffened, pulse spiking. She turned slowly, and her breath caught helplessly in her throat.

Walking towards her, clutching the familiar black jacket to her chest, was Mydei. Her hair fell loose over her shoulders, catching the light, and her cheeks were pink, but her golden eyes were determined, and she looked breathtaking.

The hallway noise dulled into a low hum.

Mydei stopped just in front of her, holding out the jacket, and her voice was soft but clear, “You… left this with me.”

Phainon’s fingers brushed against Mydei’s as she took it, and she was so sure her ears were burning red. The jacket suddenly felt impossibly heavy in her arms.

A hush fell over the hallway, and dozens of eyes were on them now, curious, nosy, waiting.

Mydei shifted on her feet, biting her lip before blurting out, too fast and too bold, “There’s this cat cafe I’ve always wanted to go to. If you’re free this evening, maybe… maybe we could go together?”

Somewhere behind Phainon, there was an audible choke. It was possibly Stelle or maybe Caelus and she didn’t care.

Phainon froze as her brain scrambled, trying to rearrange the words she’d just heard, make sure she hadn’t dreamt them. Mydei, sweet, radiant Mydei, had just asked her out.

“Y–yes! I mean–” Phainon stumbled over the words, clutching the jacket like a lifeline, “Yes, I’d love to! I’ll pick you up.”

Mydei’s face lit up like the sun breaking through clouds, and she smiled widely, tucking a strand of hair behind her ear, eyes sparkling with relief.

Then, before Phainon could catch her breath, Mydei stepped forward, grabbed her gently by the collar and pressed a quick kiss to her lips. Again.

Gasps and muffled squeals erupted from the crowd, and someone definitely dropped their coffee.

Phainon barely registered it; she was too dazed, too happy, and too dizzy with the feel of Mydei’s soft, plush lips still burning on her lips.

“See you tonight,” Mydei murmured, her blush deepening as she stepped back and gave a shy wave before disappearing into the crowd, her hair swaying behind her.

Phainon stood there, frozen, grinning like an idiot.

When she finally turned back around, the twins were waiting for her, both clutching their chests dramatically, gasping like they’d just witnessed the end of the world.

“How did you bag a baddie like her?!” Stelle shrieked, pointing a finger at him accusingly.

Caelus was too busy laughing. “I should have filmed this man, and sent it to our dad,” he wheezed, “You’re actually living in a romance anime and you're the love interest for real.”

Phainon only hugged her jacket tighter, cheeks still burning, and for once, she didn’t even try to deny it.

_______

It started barely five minutes after Mydei kissed Phainon in front of half the hallway.

By the time Phainon made it to her next class, the university’s anonymous confessions page had exploded.

By noon, it wasn’t just confessions anymore as memes started circulating, edits with sparkly filters, screenshots of anonymous comments. Even people who hadn’t been in the hallway now claimed they had seen the moment.

Meanwhile, Mydei sat in the library with her laptop open, but her attention was a thousand miles away. Her fingers kept hovering over her phone, her face hot as she scrolled through the chaos, and her cheeks ached from smiling.

She wasn’t normally one to make things public, but after last night’s dinner, after the ice cream, after the kiss in the quiet glow of the streetlamps, and then today’s boldness she didn’t know she had in her, her chest felt like it would burst if she didn’t share it.

So she did.

A photo of her strawberry ice cream from the night before, the blurred edge of a familiar black jacket sleeve in the corner, with a small caption.

maybe the best night I’ve had in a long time 🍓✨

Her notifications exploded instantly.

Across campus, sitting slouched in the gym’s locker room, Phainon only saw the post when Stelle shoved her phone into her face, “She posted this! Look!”

Phainon nearly dropped her water bottle, and her heart was doing backflips, and her grin was unstoppable.

“She, oh Titans, she actually posted,” Phainon muttered, eyes wide, “Does that mean, like, she’s okay with people knowing? She’s okay with… us?”

“Dude,” Stelle said dryly, “She just soft-launched both of you to the entire campus.”

Phainon’s ears went scarlet as she fumbled with her phone, staring at her own camera roll, at the picture she’d secretly taken last night of Mydei laughing, her hand shielding her mouth, the strawberry ice cream melting at the corners. The lighting was bad, the angle slightly tilted, but it was her, it was undeniably her.

Her thumb hovered only a moment before she posted it on her story, with no caption, only her.

Within ten minutes, the confessions page doubled in chaos.

By evening, the whole campus knew.

People smiled when they walked past. Someone even wolf-whistled when Phainon crossed the quad, which sent her sprinting in the opposite direction, ears burning.

Mydei, scrolling through the posts with her hands over her mouth, just kept giggling, cheeks glowing pink. She hadn’t expected it to feel this warm, to have everyone rooting for them.

_______

Mydei had never hated her closet more than she did that afternoon. Every hanger she pulled down was suddenly an enemy, every dress or blouse or cardigan somehow too much or too little.

“This is impossible,” she groaned, throwing yet another top across the room where it landed on her desk chair in a messy heap. “Why do I own clothes at all if none of them work?”

Castorice, perched serenely on the edge of the bed with her usual quiet poise, tilted her head. “They work fine. You just don’t think they do because you’re nervous.”

“I am not nervous,” Mydei snapped, though her hands trembled as she held up a cream sweater to her reflection. “I’m just… cautious.”

From her nest of pillows, Cipher rolled onto her side and made a loud, exaggerated gagging noise. “Cautious my ass. I guess that’s what we’re calling it when someone tries on her sixth outfit in twenty minutes because she’s so totally calm.”

Mydei flung the sweater at her, who caught it and promptly used it as a pillow, “I don’t know why you’re even here if you’re just going to be a menace.”

“Entertainment,” Cipher said simply, smirking.

Castorice, ever the mediator, rose and took Mydei gently by the shoulders. “Listen,” she said softly, looking her in the eye, “You look radiant in anything you put on. She’s not going to care if it’s jeans or a skirt, she’s only going to care about you.”

Mydei’s throat tightened as she nodded, biting her lip as if that could hold back her emotions, and returned to the closet. Finally, after what felt like hours, she settled on a soft blouse tucked into a flowing skirt, paired with the delicate necklace she always wore when she needed courage. She stared at her reflection and she didn’t hate it.

Just as she was smoothing down the skirt with shaking hands, her phone buzzed and her heart leapt into her throat. 

“She’s here,” she whispered, almost in disbelief.

Then louder, panicked, “She’s here!”

She bolted for the door, almost tripping on her own heels as she ran down the stairs. Behind her, Cipher cupped her hands around her mouth and called after her, “Don’t do anything I wouldn’t do! Don't forget to use protection!” followed by a dramatic retching noise. Castorice’s voice, calmer but firmer, rang out above it, “Good luck and have fun!”

Mydei barely heard them.

At the bottom of the stairs, standing just outside the doorway, was Phainon.

She looked… awkward. Adorable, even, with one arm tucked stiffly behind her back, the other hovering like she wasn’t sure what to do with it. Her blue eyes flickered nervously to the side until she noticed Mydei, and then, oh Titans, that smile was wide and real.

Suddenly, Mydei remembered her last so-called date. The one who didn't even show up on time, the one who left her on read, and the one who still hasn't bothered to reply to her. The memory flared in sharp contrast to the sight before her now, Phainon, early, waiting, looking like she’d been rehearsing this moment for hours.

Mydei’s chest flooded with warmth so quickly it almost made her dizzy. Without thinking and without hesitating, she closed the space between them and launched herself forward, wrapping her arms tight around Phainon’s neck.

The kiss was soft, brief, but it stunned Phainon anyway.

When Mydei pulled back, she caught the dazed expression on Phainon’s face, the wide eyes, the parted lips, and the faintest red climbing her ears. She looked like someone who had just been handed the world and didn’t know what to do with it. Mydei’s heart tumbled, and inside she giggled at how utterly puppy-like Phainon was in that moment.

“You… you look so pretty,” Phainon blurted, her voice rough with nerves, and then, as if remembering why she’d been standing so stiffly, she pulled her arm from behind her back and revealed a small bouquet, myrtles and forget-me-nots, tied together with a ribbon that looked like it had been knotted and unknotted three times from nerves.

Mydei froze, heat rushing up her neck, across her cheeks, flooding her entire body as she bit her lip hard to keep the squeal trapped in her throat. Behind her, she could hear Cipher’s obnoxious gagging through the open window upstairs, but for once she didn’t care.

She reached out, accepting the bouquet with both hands as if it were something fragile, precious. “Thank you,” she whispered, before leaning in and brushing the lightest kiss against Phainon’s cheek.

Phainon went scarlet all over again, grinning so wide it was almost ridiculous.

“So,” Mydei said, tucking a strand of hair behind her ear, her smile blooming despite her best efforts to play it cool, “Are we ready to go?”

Phainon nodded so quickly it looked like she might give herself whiplash, “Yes–yes, I'm ready! Totally ready.”

And then, with a boldness Mydei didn’t know she had, reached down and laced her fingers through Mydei’s, holding tight as though she might float away otherwise.

Together, bouquet in hand, hearts thundering, they walked toward the cafe.

_______

“What?!”

“How sweet! I suppose we'd better start making arrangements and calls, Eurypon. I can't wait to meet her, my cub.“
